candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — nutrition, feeding and comfort-related nursing interventions tailored to client needs and symptoms.
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate cancer cachexia from simple inadequate intake and support individualized multidisciplinary management that includes, but is not limited to, dietitian-guided nutrition intervention.

options.A: Cachexia is a complex wasting syndrome that is not fully reversed by nutrition alone; care should address symptoms and medical contributors while using individualized nutrition support, often with a registered dietitian.
options.B: Cachexia is caused only by inadequate calorie intake, so increasing food intake is sufficient to reverse the syndrome in most clients.
options.C: Nutrition support has no role in cachexia, so dietary assessment and symptom-related eating problems should not be addressed.
options.D: Every client with cachexia should receive the same high-calorie meal plan regardless of appetite, symptoms, cancer type, or goals of care.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. NCI describes cancer cachexia as a wasting syndrome with loss of skeletal muscle and fat that, unlike simple malnutrition, cannot be reversed with nutrition support alone. Inflammation, metabolic changes, reduced intake, and symptom burden may contribute. NCI recommends multidisciplinary management and notes that registered dietitians can provide individualized nutrition counseling and strategies. B is incorrect because inadequate calories are not the sole mechanism and increased intake alone does not reliably reverse cachexia. C is incorrect because nutrition assessment and support remain clinically useful even though they are not sufficient by themselves. D is incorrect because nutrition intervention should be individualized rather than a single universal meal plan.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Cancer cachexia is multifactorial and not reversed by nutrition support alone; individualized multidisciplinary care and registered-dietitian nutrition support remain appropriate.

candidate.stem: The family of a client with advanced cancer and diagnosed cachexia says, 'If we can just make him eat enough calories, the muscle loss should reverse.' Which response by the nurse is most accurate?
